title: Where Is Manhattan's Official Culture? Cultural Organizations, City Blocks, and Subway Access
gallery_text: This map counts, block by block, the cultural organizations listed in New York City's Department of Cultural Affairs directory, outlines Manhattan's neighborhoods, and overlays subway stations with a 5-minute walking radius. Midtown–Times Square holds 149 listed organizations, more than three times as many as Tribeca (45) or either half of Harlem (31 and 28), raising the question of whether this maps where culture happens or only where it is officially registered and easy to reach.
description:
Datasets from NYC Open Data and data.ny.gov:

DCLA Cultural Organizations (NYC Department of Cultural Affairs, u35m-9t32; published 2018, last updated 2021). A directory of organizations the agency works with, located by mailing address. 267 of 2,535 entries have no coordinates, and some addresses are "c/o" mailing addresses. Used here as a map of institutional culture per city block and neighborhood.
MTA Subway Stations (MTA, data.ny.gov, 39hk-dx4f; published 2024). A reference list of stations with location, lines, structure type, and ADA accessibility. Used here to draw a 5-minute walking radius (~0.75 mile, straight-line) around each station.
Base geography: 2020 Census Blocks (wmsu-5muw) and 2020 Neighborhood Tabulation Areas (9nt8-h7nd), both by NYC Department of City Planning. They were made for reporting census statistics; I use them here as city blocks and neighborhood outlines. Each organization was assigned to the nearest block within 150 ft of its geocoded address, then counted per block and per neighborhood. 

Projection: NAD83 / New York State Plane, Long Island (EPSG:2263).
Design: dark background / glowing color scale / annotated labels.
Code written and debugged with AI assistance (Claude).
